## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10) is the concluding discourse of the fifth chapter (*Soṇavagga*) of the Pali Udāna [Masefield 1997]. Set in Jeta's Grove at Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery in Sāvatthī, the brief narrative depicts the Buddha observing the venerable Cūḷapanthaka seated in quiet meditation nearby, legs crossed and body held upright, with mindfulness firmly established before him [Masefield 1997]. Moved by this sight, the Buddha utters an inspired verse (*udāna*) extolling the practitioner who remains steadfast in body and mind whether standing, sitting, or lying down; by applying and resolving upon mindfulness (*etaṁ satiṁ bhikkhu adhiṭṭhahāno*), the monk gains progressive spiritual attainment and passes beyond the reach of the King of Death [Lim 2009; Masefield 1997]. In modern philological study, this verse is cited for its early canonical usage of the participle *adhiṭṭhahāna* in the sense of setting up or maintaining resolute mindfulness [Lim 2009].
